paragraphs: Last Saturday, Tom and I went to the bike shop near the market. The shop was small, but it was full of bikes. Tom needed a new light for his bike, and I wanted to see the shop. Mia's dad works there, but he was in the back room. A young woman stood behind the desk. She was the shop assistant, and she studied at college on weekdays. "Good morning," she said. "Can I help you?"

"Yes, please," said Tom. "I need a light for my bike." "We have two kinds," said the assistant. "This one is small, and that one is strong." "Which one is better for riding at night?" asked Tom. "The strong one," she said. "You can see the whole road with it." "How much does it cost?" asked Tom. "It costs two hundred baht," she said. "The small one costs one hundred baht." "I will take the strong one," said Tom.

"Would you like a helmet, too?" asked the assistant. "My old helmet is too small," said Tom. The assistant opened a file on the computer. "We have one helmet in your size," she said. "It is blue, and it is three hundred baht." "Do you want to try it on?" she asked. Tom put it on, and it was comfortable. "It is perfect," he said.

"Is the shop open all day?" I asked. "No, we shut at one o'clock on Saturday," said the assistant. "It is half past twelve now." "Nobody else is in the shop, so we have time." "Every customer gets a free check for the wheels." She went outside and looked at the wheels of Tom's bike. She pushed each wheel with her hand, and it turned well. "They are fine," she said.

"Do you pay with cash or with a card?" asked the assistant. "I pay with cash," said Tom. He gave her five hundred baht. She gave him a receipt and a small bag. I looked at the red bikes while Tom paid. "Thank you, and have a nice day," she said. Tom smiled, and we rode home.
